confirmed.evidence: The justification's FACTS check out: the Spellshifter action is genuinely absent from our corpus (name search across all 79 buckets returns only feats/shift-spell — the level-14 wizard feat, aonId feat-2731, whose printed text is about moving a spell's area), so pointing at it would be the defect. But the conclusion does not follow. Grepping the id across ALL of src/ returns ZERO hits — no registry entry, no branch in derive.ts or build.ts — and scripts/data/effect-backfill.json does not carry it either. The record holds one `note` string and nothing else. And the app HAS the lane: `grantsActions` is live on 148 feat records pointing into the 879-entry `actions` bucket (e.g. quick-alchemy, brightness-seeker, aegis-of-arnisant), so this is an un-imported record, not an unmodellable clause.
confirmed.theyDeliver: A discrete, named ability entry for the Shift Spell action on the character's sheet, carried by an explicit grant on the dedication.
confirmed.weDeliver: The dedication feat plus a one-line note. No Shift Spell entry appears anywhere on the sheet; the rules are readable only by opening the dedication's own description.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Author a Spellshifter "Shift Spell" record in core.json's `actions` bucket under an id distinct from `shift-spell` (plus the Share the Burden spellshift), then add `grantsActions: ['<new-id>']` to feats/spellshifter-dedication — the same lane the other 148 granted actions already use.

confirmed.evidence: The carrier claim is half true and I confirmed the working half: the record carries `choice { flag: 'firstHeritage', from: { type: 'heritage', ancestry: 'dragonet' } }` plus `secondHeritage: true`, resolved by `secondHeritageIdOf` (src/rules/build.ts:411-418) and read at roughly a dozen sites. MEASURED: a dragonet with a versatile heritage who takes this feat and names Tidepool Dragonet gets swim 15 and the extra language. But src/rules/build.ts:6083-6087 reads heritage `innateSpells` from `build.heritageId` ONLY — `secondHeritageId` is absent from that one loop, unlike the sibling loops at :3033, :4729, :5469 and :5928. MEASURED: naming Homing Drake produces NO spellcasting entry at all; the at-will arcane Know the Way cantrip that heritage prints (heritages.homing-drake.innateSpells) is silently dropped.
confirmed.theyDeliver: All five options' mechanical content, including the drake option's at-will arcane cantrip, because their side copies each heritage's effects into the option.
confirmed.weDeliver: Speeds, languages and creature traits from the named heritage — but no innate spells, so the drake option delivers nothing at all.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add `secondHeritageId` to the heritage innate-spell loop at src/rules/build.ts:6083, using the same `for (const hid of [build.heritageId, secondHeritageId])` shape already used at build.ts:3033, :4729, :5469 and :5928.

confirmed.evidence: The two named vocabulary differences ARE equivalent (same global innate-proficiency rule as labyrinthine-echoes). The problem is what the cited backfill left behind. It added an `effectChoices` picker to the record — `moon-weavers-spell`, two options, each granting one occult innate spell at 1/day — but did NOT remove the pre-existing pick-a-spell registry entry at src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts:98. Both lanes are live: src/builder/Builder.tsx:2172-2192 renders a SECOND picker for any feat present in that registry, alongside the effectChoices picker, and src/rules/build.ts pushes both answers into innateGrants (:6128-6130 for the choice, :6132-6150 for the registry pick), deduping only by spell id. MEASURED by building a sarangay who answers one picker Illusory Object and the other Invisible Item: the innate entry comes back holding BOTH at rank 1. Answering only one picker gives the correct single spell.
confirmed.theyDeliver: One occult innate spell, once per day, chosen from the two the clause names.
confirmed.weDeliver: Two separate prompts for one clause, and — if the player answers both differently — two occult innate spells at 1/day each.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Delete the `'the-moon-weavers-art'` entry from src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts:98 now that the record's own `effectChoices` carries the pick; and add a guard so no record can appear in FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS and in `effectChoices` with an innateSpells grant at the same time.

confirmed.evidence: The carrier claim is true and I verified the parts it names: `gateForks` / `gateExpands` are BuildState fields (src/rules/build.ts:179-181), rendered by src/builder/shared.tsx:3332-3392, applied at build.ts:3928-3939 and build.ts:6398 / src/rules/kineticElements.ts:70, and the forked element does reach `classChoices` (measured: fire+water+air). But the two branches do not hand over the same things. The printed Fork the Path clause is *"Add a new element of your choice... Gain an impulse feat of your level or lower with the trait of that element"*, and their encoding nests exactly that second pick under the fork branch. Ours renders no picker for it (shared.tsx:3360 gates the impulse sub-pick on `cur === ''`, i.e. only when NOT forking) and build.ts:3931 explicitly early-continues on a recorded fork with the comment "forked → no bonus impulse". MEASURED at level 5 with fire+water gates: Expand the Portal yields 1 granted feat (flying-flame); Fork the Path yields 0 granted feats.
confirmed.theyDeliver: An impulse feat on BOTH branches — element-matched and non-composite on the fork branch — in addition to the new element.
confirmed.weDeliver: An impulse feat only on the Expand branch. A kineticist who forks gets the element and no feat, and is short up to four impulse feats by 17th level.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a fork-side impulse pick (e.g. `gateForkImpulses`, keyed by threshold level like the other two maps, offered filtered to the newly-forked element's trait and excluding composite impulses), render it in src/builder/shared.tsx beside the existing fork select, and stop the early-continue at src/rules/build.ts:3931 from swallowing the fork branch's feat.

confirmed.theyDeliver: From 9th level the chosen spell (Gentle Landing or Jump) is cast as a 3rd-rank innate spell, and from 12th the innate DC/attack step to expert.
confirmed.weDeliver: The chosen spell is cast at its base 1st rank at every level from 5 to 20; only the expert step arrives.
confirmed.suggestedFix: CantripPickSpec in src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts carries no rank/heighten field and build.ts:6148 pushes a bare {spellId, tradition}. Either add `rank`/`heightenAt` to CantripPickSpec and honour it in that push, or move colugos-traversal off the pick lane onto an `effectChoices` whose two options each grant innateSpells with heightenAt:[{level:9, rank:3}] — the shape stem-the-tide already uses.
confirmed.evidence: Printed (core-descriptions feats/colugos-traversal): 'You can cast your choice of Gentle Landing or Jump as a primal innate spell once per day. At 9th level, these spells are heightened to 3rd rank.' Ours is src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts:59, whose own file header states 'exact feat heightening is not modeled'. Both spells are rank 1 in core.json, and castRank (src/rules/build.ts:6171-6200) returns max(base, g.rank ?? base) with no rank, no heightenAt and no heightenHalfLevel on the pushed grant — I grepped `heightenHalfLevel` across src/, scripts/ and core.json and it appears on 339 records, none of them this one, contradicting the justification's claim that 'ours carries heightenHalfLevel on the grant'. The justification also quotes Stem the Tide's 7th-level-and-every-2-levels sentence, which is not this feat's text. Theirs (ability_block 35362) has three level branches (<9, 9-11, >=12) each re-granting the spell, so a 9th-level player on their side casts it at 3rd rank.

The justification claims our `unarmedTraits` rider steps the die and adds parry. It does not. feats/spirit-warrior-dedication's entire rider is `[{ remove: ['nonlethal'] }]` (authored at scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:51867). `spirit-warrior` appears NOWHERE in src/ — no registry, no derive/build branch — and its only other backfill rows are `grantsActions:['overwhelming-combination']` and `actionCost`. The engine fully supports the missing half: UnarmedRider (src/rules/types.ts:528-577) has `match`, `stepDie` and `add`, and feats/steelhoof already uses `{match:['hoof'], stepDie:true}`.
confirmed.theyDeliver: A fist that is already 1d6 and already has the parry trait, handed over as a pre-modified unarmed attack.
confirmed.weDeliver: A fist that is still 1d4 and has no parry trait; only the nonlethal trait is stripped.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Extend the `unarmedTraits` value for feats/spirit-warrior-dedication in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json (row at line 51867) to `[{ remove: ['nonlethal'] }, { match: ['fist'], stepDie: true, add: ['parry'] }]` so it survives `npm run data`.

confirmed.evidence: The record uses the WRONG resource. feats/firework-technician-dedication carries `advancedAlchemy: { items: 4 }`, which src/rules/build.ts:4834-4861 turns into `character.advancedAlchemy = { max: 4 }` — the Advanced Alchemy DAILY PREPARED-ITEM budget. But the printed clause is the Quick Alchemy one, identical in wording to Alchemist Dedication and Wandering Chef Dedication, both of which the app models correctly and differently: `grantsActions: ['quick-alchemy']` on the record plus a feat-gated `versatile-vials` counter with `maxBase: 4` in src/rules/classResources.ts:80-97. There is no such counter gated on firework-technician-dedication, and the record does not grant quick-alchemy. src/sheet/AlchemyPanel.tsx:30-47 confirms the consequence: `hasAdvanced` is true so the panel prints a "prepared 0/4" budget the archetype should not have, while `vialDef` resolves to undefined and the vial line falls back to 2 + Int.
confirmed.theyDeliver: Four pyrotechnic versatile vials plus the Quick Alchemy benefits, so the player has the vial resource the Launch Fireworks action and fireworks consumables are meant to spend.
confirmed.weDeliver: No Quick Alchemy action, no 4-vial resource (the panel falls back to 2 + Int), and instead an Advanced Alchemy prepared-item budget of 4 that the printed feat never grants.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Mirror the alchemist-dedication treatment: add a `versatile-vials` entry in src/rules/classResources.ts (alchemist bucket) with `maxBase: 4, maxPerLevel: 0, feat: 'firework-technician-dedication'`, add `quick-alchemy` to the record's `grantsActions`, and drop `advancedAlchemy: { items: 4 }` from the feats/firework-technician-dedication row in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json.

confirmed.evidence: The justification's premise is false and the mechanic is missing. False premise: a `focus` field on a class feature IS read — src/rules/build.ts:3008 sums `content.classFeatures[fid].focusPoolBonus` over `classFeatureIdsOwned` (which includes the chosen subclass id) and src/rules/build.ts:3702 adds it to the animist pool, so the Medium option could carry it. Missing mechanic: I read their row directly and their focus operation here belongs to the MEDIUM practice — one extra focus point once the character is 9th level or higher AND does not have Circle of Spirits. Our animist branch (src/rules/build.ts:3681-3702) has only the flat 1/7/15 ladder plus a `focusSeen.has('circle-of-spirits')` clause; there is no Medium branch, and classes.animist.subclass.options['medium'] carries description prose only, no grant. The Medium's Dual Invocation text (pool = number of focus spells or number of PRIMARY apparitions, whichever is higher, max 3) is therefore unmodelled, including the two-primary-apparitions half.
confirmed.theyDeliver: A Medium-practice animist at levels 9-14 has 3 Focus Points (base 1 + the third-apparition point + the Medium's own point), suppressed only if they already have Circle of Spirits.
confirmed.weDeliver: A Medium-practice animist at levels 9-14 has 2 Focus Points — identical to every other practice, because nothing reads the practice choice.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a Medium branch beside the existing Circle of Spirits clause in the animist section of src/rules/build.ts (~line 3690): when `build.subclassId === 'medium'` and level >= 9 and the character lacks circle-of-spirits, raise poolMax the same way (`Math.max(poolMax, pointCostingKnown.length, 2)`), so the printed "whichever is higher" reading lands. Alternatively author `focusPoolBonus` on the medium subclass record, which build.ts:3008 already reads.

confirmed.theyDeliver: A swashbuckler picking their bonus skill feat at 3rd/7th/15th is offered feats for Acrobatics OR for the skill their style granted — so a Braggart can take an Intimidation feat, a Battledancer a Performance feat, and so on.
confirmed.weDeliver: Only Acrobatics feats (plus feats that name no skill at all). Every style skill — Performance, Intimidation, Deception, Athletics, Diplomacy — is filtered OUT of the slot, so a Braggart swashbuckler cannot put an Intimidation feat in the slot the rules reserve for exactly that.
confirmed.evidence: The bonus-skill-INCREASE half of the justification is true: public/core.json classes/swashbuckler.bonusSkillIncreaseLevels = [3,7,15], read at src/rules/build.ts:2730 and 2735 and surfaced at build.ts:7684. The bonus skill-FEAT slot exists too: classes/swashbuckler.featProgression.skill = [2,3,4,6,7,8,10,12,14,15,16,18,20]. But the narrowing half is not what the justification says. classes/swashbuckler.restrictedSkillFeatLevels = {levels:[3,7,15], skills:['acrobatics'], includeSubclassGrantedSkills:true, featureId:'stylish-tricks', reason:'...'} — and includeSubclassGrantedSkills HAS NO READER. Grepping the whole tree finds it only twice: the type declaration at src/rules/types.ts:3145 and the authored value at scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:134569. The only consumer of the field, src/rules/featSlots.ts:183-192, builds its allowed set from restrict.skills plus restrict.abilities and never looks at the flag; swashbuckler sets no abilities list, so allowed = {acrobatics} alone. This is the write-only-field-with-no-reader shape. The owner's picker-filtering exception covers our CHOOSING to filter in the slot rather than on the record — it does not cover filtering out options the printed rule allows.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In src/rules/featSlots.ts inside the restrictedSkillFeatLevels block (around line 186), when restrict.includeSubclassGrantedSkills is set, add the skills granted by the character's chosen subclass option (core.json classes/<id>.subclass.options[].grants.skills — e.g. battledancer -> performance, braggart -> intimidation) to the `allowed` set before the named.some() test. Investigator's entry needs the same flag for correctness even though its ability list already covers every methodology skill.

confirmed.theyDeliver: TWO resistance entries: the all-damage-except-force/vitality/ghost-touch resistance at 1, rising to 2 at 10th and 3 at 16th; AND a separate resistance against non-magical damage at 2, rising to 4 at 10th and 5 at 16th. Both are real numbers on their defences.
confirmed.weDeliver: Only the first entry. A ghost-archetype character hit by a non-magical weapon reduces damage by 1/2/3 on our sheet where the rules (and their sheet) give 2/4/5.
confirmed.evidence: public/core.json feats/ghostly-resistance carries a single resistance: {type:'all-damage', value:'floor((@actor.level+2)/6)', condition:'except force, vitality, and damage from a ghost touch weapon (or anything acting as one)'}. The formula is correct for the first half (level 4->1, 10->2, 16->3), but the printed second half — 'This resistance increases to 2 if the source is non-magical... at 10th level, 2, or 4 if non-magical... at 16th, 3, or 5 if non-magical' (core-descriptions.json feats/ghostly-resistance, AoN feat-3498) — has no carrier anywhere. scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:8213 (the durable source, since anything not there dies at the next `npm run data`) writes that ONE entry and nothing else; grepping ghostly-resistance across all of src/ returns zero hits, so there is no situationalBonuses star, no RECORD_MARKERS note and no second resistance row. The justification only ever discussed the exception-in-the-type-string vs exception-as-condition shape and never mentions the doubled non-magical value at all.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a second entry to feats/ghostly-resistance.resistances in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json: {type:'physical' is wrong here — use a non-magical-source entry, e.g. type:'all-damage', value:'2*floor((@actor.level+2)/6)' at levels 4-9 and the printed 4/5 steps thereafter, condition:'against non-magical sources; still excludes force, vitality and ghost touch'}. The printed ladder is 2/4/5 rather than a clean double at 16th, so author it as an explicit level formula, e.g. floor((@actor.level+2)/6) mapped 1->2, 2->4, 3->5.

confirmed.theyDeliver: The base resistance 3 to the chosen physical type (adamantine bypasses), AND the record's Enhancement tier as a second menu: either resistance 3 to ALL physical damage (adamantine still bypasses), or a further increase to the already-chosen type.
confirmed.weDeliver: Only the base resistance 3 to the chosen type. The Enhancement clause reaches the player as description text and nothing else — and because the feat is not registered as enhanceable, it is not even offered as a target when the character takes Lesser or Greater Augmentation.
confirmed.evidence: The base half matches exactly: public/core.json feats/hardened-chassis.choice offers bludgeoning/piercing/slashing, each granting {value:3, condition:'except against adamantine weapons and unarmed attacks'}, applied through the same build.ts:4768-4772 -> applyAlwaysOn -> mergeEffect path as mortification. The Enhancement is the gap. Our own printed text on the record (core-descriptions.json feats/hardened-chassis) carries it: 'Enhancement ... you gain resistance 3 to all physical damage, or your chosen resistance increases to a value equal to half your level (minimum 3)'. The engine HAS a route for this — src/rules/build.ts:4723-4726 applies content.feats[x].enhancement.grant, and build.ts:4695-4703 builds the list from a feat with an enhancementPicker — but only six feats carry an `enhancement` field (automaton-armament, arcane-communication, arcane-eye, automaton-lore, powerful-tail, undead-hunter) and hardened-chassis is not one of them; grepping hardened-chassis across src/ and test/ returns nothing, and scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:136938 writes only the three-option base choice. build.ts:4700 skips any answer whose feat has no `enhancement`, so the two Augmentation feats (lesser-augmentation, greater-augmentation) cannot even list it. The justification's claim that 'the upgrade is the upgrading record's business' is false: the upgrade is printed on THIS record and no other record on our side carries it.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add an `enhancement` block to feats/hardened-chassis in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json in the shape build.ts:4723-4726 reads. Because the tier is itself a two-way choice, author it the way automaton-lore does (enhancement.choiceIds pointing at an effectChoices group) with option A granting {type:'physical', value:3, condition:'except against adamantine weapons and unarmed attacks'} and option B raising the already-chosen type to 'max(3,floor(@actor.level/2))'. Do NOT author it as a one-option effectChoices picker — resolvePick auto-applies a lone unanswered option (build.ts:4558).

confirmed.theyDeliver: A +1 bonus to seven knowledge skills, each op carrying a condition limiting it to Recall Knowledge checks about the value of items, gems and precious metals.
confirmed.weDeliver: Nothing. public/core.json items/merchants-scale ships description "", no `situational` entry and no skill grant — and even a correctly authored star would be inert, because an item's situational bonuses are admitted only while the row is equipped/worn/invested (explain.ts characterSituationalIds) and no equip control renders for an untraited `equipment` item (InventoryTab.tsx equipControl / isEquippable, per the measurements recorded in work/wg-lane-backlog.md:430-460).
confirmed.evidence: Index 137, packet bucket AUTHORISED. I read the record and the cited file. The half of the justification about NOT copying their sentence is genuinely right: their dump is GPL-3.0, and work/wg-lane-backlog.md:405-425 records that the AoN mirror docs equipment-2734 and equipment-34, live AoN for both ids, and the Foundry record are all stat-block stubs with no body, so the printed paragraph cannot be sourced anywhere this project may use. The file also says exactly what the settle claims it says, including 'this settle closes the +1, not the description'. But the audit question is what the player receives, and on our side that is zero across all seven silenced keys — the backlog itself calls it 'its own defect'. It does not fit AUTHORISED ground (a) (we cannot read the printed text, so their data cannot be shown to contradict it), (b), or (c) (there is no star to point at). Recording it as DIVERGENT so the gap stays visible; the ruling against adopting their flat +1 verbatim stands and should not be reversed.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Three steps, in order: (1) add a Hold/Use route for `equipment`-typed items whose `usage` is `held-in-*` in src/sheet/InventoryTab.tsx, or the rest is inert; (2) source the Player Core pg. 290 paragraph from the physical book — not from their dump, not from PF1 — and put it in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json; (3) add one starred conditional per named skill under 'merchants-scale' in FEAT_SITUATIONAL (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts), in the merchants-guile shape.

confirmed.theyDeliver: A named one-action ability called Shift Spell added to the character, carrying the Shift Spell rules text with the Share the Burden spellshift injected into it — so it appears on their sheet as an action with an action cost, not as a paragraph inside the feat.
confirmed.weDeliver: Nothing structured. feats/spellshifter-dedication has no `grantsActions`, no `grantsFeats`, no `grantsClassFeatures` — only a one-line `note` plus the imported description text.
confirmed.evidence: Every factual claim in the justification checks out: I searched all 78 buckets of public/core.json and the only record named Shift Spell is feats/shift-spell, a level-14 wizard feat whose text moves an ongoing spell's area 120 feet — a different ability that merely shares the name. Pointing at it would indeed be the defect. And the archetype really is prose-only: only three records carry `archetype: 'spellshifter'` (the dedication, analyze-magic, reactive-spellshift), none with grantsActions. But 'the record does not exist in our corpus' is a description of a gap, not a reason the player gets the same thing. The app authors records when the corpus lacks them — stances/haft-striker-stance and all 18 werecreature battle forms carry `aonOrigin: 'authored'` — so this is buildable, and until it is built their player has an action on the sheet and ours has a paragraph.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Author an `actions` bucket record for the archetype's Shift Spell (1 action, concentrate + manipulate, with the Arcana-check text) plus the Share the Burden spellshift, mark it `aonOrigin: 'authored'`, and set `grantsActions: ['<that id>']` on feats/spellshifter-dedication — the same route already used for the werecreature battle forms and the haft-striker stance. Do NOT reinstate any grant pointing at feats/shift-spell.

confirmed.theyDeliver: A second, computed question on the record: whether the feat's Enhancement tier is active. Answering it either turns the single-type resistance into resistance 3 against ALL physical damage, or raises the chosen type's resistance — and their engine writes the resulting resistance onto the character.
confirmed.weDeliver: The three printed damage types only. feats/hardened-chassis has NO `enhancement` field (only six automaton feats do: automaton-armament, arcane-communication, arcane-eye, automaton-lore, powerful-tail, undead-hunter), and feats/lesser-augmentation and feats/greater-augmentation list Hardened Chassis with the note 'Prose benefit - read this feat's Enhancement entry and apply it in play; the app does not compute it.'
confirmed.evidence: The base half is genuinely matched: public/core.json feats/hardened-chassis `choice` (flag `hardenedChassisDamage`) has three options each granting resistance 3 with the adamantine exception, applied at src/rules/build.ts:4768-4772 (a feat's plain choice grant). The justification's read of their extra options is also correct — they are the Enhancement question, not extra damage types. What is NOT correct is the inference drawn from it. The justification says 'on our side an upgrade is the upgrading record's business', which implies the upgrading record delivers it; it does not. The enhancement lane exists and works (src/rules/build.ts:4695-4725 resolves the augmentation picker and applies `enhancement.grant`, with `enhancement.choiceIds` gating a tier-only sub-question — automaton-lore uses exactly that shape), but hardened-chassis was never authored into it. I also checked scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:136937 — it backfills only the `choice` field for this record, no enhancement. So an automaton with Lesser or Greater Augmentation pointed at Hardened Chassis gets a computed resistance on their sheet and a 'do it yourself' note on ours.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add an `enhancement` block to feats/hardened-chassis in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json with `choiceIds: ['<new effectChoices id>']` and a two-option effectChoices entry for the printed branches — resistance 3 to all physical damage (adamantine still bypasses), or the already-chosen type raised to max(3, floor(level/2)) — then change the hardened-chassis option note in feats/lesser-augmentation and feats/greater-augmentation from 'Prose benefit …' to the 'Computed on your sheet' wording the other six use.

confirmed.theyDeliver: An at-will innate primal cantrip that is the CURRENT printing: a 5-foot burst at 30 feet, basic Reflex save, 1d8 damage, heightening by +1d8 every 2 ranks, retyped to the chosen energy.
confirmed.weDeliver: An at-will innate primal cantrip pointing at our `acid-splash` record, which our own corpus stamps edition 'superseded': a single-target SPELL ATTACK at 30 feet, 1d6 plus splash plus persistent on a crit, with fixed heightening at ranks 3/5/7/9.
confirmed.evidence: feats.elemental-wrath carries innateSpells [{spellId:'acid-splash'}] plus four effectChoices branches all granting the same 'acid-splash' id. Our corpus ships BOTH records side by side: spells['acid-splash'] has edition 'superseded', traits include 'attack', targets '1 creature', baseDamage 1d6, fixed heightening; spells['caustic-blast'] has edition 'remaster', area '5-foot burst', save {reflex, basic:true}, baseDamage 1d8, interval heightening. build.ts:2382-2384 states that edition 'superseded' is ALWAYS hidden from pickers, so this grant hands the player a record the app otherwise refuses to offer. The justification's premise ("one spell, two printings") is true of the NAMES but false of the two records we actually ship - they are mechanically different spells, and the grant points at the retired one.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Repoint feats.elemental-wrath.innateSpells[0].spellId and all four effectChoices[0].options[].grant.innateSpells[0].spellId from 'acid-splash' to 'caustic-blast' (in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, so it survives `npm run data`). Keep the spellNotes rider; update its spellId to match.

confirmed.theyDeliver: The Quick Alchemy benefits package - Alchemical Crafting, the Quick Alchemy activity, and a stock of versatile vials created at daily preparations - plus the pyrotechnic vial item itself, so the 1-vial cost of Launch Fireworks has a resource to spend.
confirmed.weDeliver: An Advanced Alchemy prepared-item budget of 4 (a different subsystem the printed feat does not grant) and NO versatile-vial counter at all, so Launch Fireworks has nothing to spend and the vial chip never appears on the sheet.
confirmed.evidence: feats.firework-technician-dedication carries advancedAlchemy {items:4}, which build.ts:4834-4861 turns into character.advancedAlchemy.max = 4 - the daily PREPARED-ITEM budget shown in AlchemyPanel, not vials. Versatile vials are a separate resource, and every definition of it lives in src/rules/classResources.ts:60, :81 and :97, gated on classId 'alchemist' or the feats 'alchemist-dedication' / 'wandering-chef-dedication'. resourcesForCharacter (classResources.ts:202-214) admits an ungated entry only when classId === 'alchemist', so a firework technician matches none of the three: MainTab.tsx:311 hasVersatileVials is false, and AlchemyPanel.tsx:43-45 finds no vialDef and silently falls back to 2 + Int. Launch Fireworks is present (grantsActions) and Fireworks Lore is present (featGrantsAuto.ts:299), so the gap is specifically the vial resource.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a fourth 'versatile-vials' entry in src/rules/classResources.ts under the alchemist bucket, gated `feat: 'firework-technician-dedication'`, maxBase 4, maxPerLevel 0, refresh 'rest', with a note saying the vials are pyrotechnic and can be replenished during exploration - exactly the shape already used for 'alchemist-dedication' and 'wandering-chef-dedication'. summary:
# Settle audit → engineer work list

**Scope.** 18 divergent settle entries covering **14 distinct records**. Four records were reported twice under different gates and are merged here into one work item each: `spellshifter-dedication` (KINDS + IDENTITY), `hardened-chassis` (VALUES + IDENTITY), `spirit-warrior-dedication` (KINDS + IDENTITY), `firework-technician-dedication` (KINDS + IDENTITY). Nothing came back UNSURE, but six items carry a decision the engineer cannot make alone — those are collected in §3.

I re-verified the load-bearing facts in the repo before writing the fixes; four suggested fixes as written would not have worked, and those corrections are marked **⚠ FIX AS WRITTEN IS WRONG**.

---

## 1. Confirmed divergences, ordered by what a player loses

### P1 — a missing grant or a wrong number

---

**1. `gates-threshold` — a forking kineticist loses up to four impulse feats** (KINDS)

- **They deliver:** an impulse feat on *both* threshold branches. Fork the Path hands over the new element **and** a matching, non-composite impulse feat.
- **We deliver:** an impulse feat on the Expand branch only. Measured at level 5 with fire+water gates: Expand yields one granted feat, Fork yields zero. Across the four thresholds a fork-heavy kineticist is short up to four feats by 17th.
- **Fix:** add a fork-side impulse pick (`gateForkImpulses`, keyed by threshold level like the existing two maps), offered filtered to the newly-forked element's trait and excluding composite impulses; render it in `src/builder/shared.tsx` beside the fork select (the sub-pick is currently gated on `cur === ''` at ~:3360, i.e. only when *not* forking); and remove the early-`continue` at `src/rules/build.ts:3931` whose comment reads "forked → no bonus impulse", which swallows the fork branch's feat.
- **Guard:** assert that every recorded gate threshold answer, on either branch, produces exactly one granted impulse feat.

---

**2. `firework-technician-dedication` — no vial resource, plus a budget from the wrong subsystem** (KINDS + IDENTITY)

- **They deliver:** the Quick Alchemy package — the crafting feat, the Quick Alchemy activity, and four versatile vials made at daily preparations, pyrotechnic-flavoured. The archetype's own action has a resource to spend.
- **We deliver:** `advancedAlchemy: { items: 4 }`, which `build.ts:4834-4861` turns into an Advanced Alchemy **prepared-item** budget — a different subsystem the printed feat never grants. No Quick Alchemy action, no vial counter. `AlchemyPanel.tsx` prints a "prepared 0/4" budget that shouldn't exist and falls back to `2 + Int` for vials because `vialDef` resolves undefined.
- **Confirming detail I found in the record itself:** `feats/firework-technician-dedication.note` already reads that the character's versatile vials are pyrotechnic — the record narrates a resource the character does not have.
- **Fix (mirror the alchemist-dedication treatment exactly):**
  1. add a fourth `versatile-vials` entry in `src/rules/classResources.ts` under the alchemist bucket, gated `feat: 'firework-technician-dedication'`, `maxBase: 4`, `maxPerLevel: 0`, refresh `rest`;
  2. add `quick-alchemy` to the record's `grantsActions` (it currently holds only `launch-fireworks`);
  3. drop `advancedAlchemy: { items: 4 }` from the record's row in `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json`.
- **Note:** `resourcesForCharacter` (`classResources.ts:202-214`) admits an ungated entry only when `classId === 'alchemist'`, so the gate must be the feat id — an ungated entry will not fire for an archetype.

---

**3. `hardened-chassis` — the whole Enhancement tier is missing, and it blocks two other feats** (VALUES + IDENTITY)

- **They deliver:** the base resistance 3 to the chosen physical type (adamantine bypasses) **and** a second, computed question for the Enhancement tier: either resistance 3 to *all* physical damage, or the already-chosen type raised to half level (min 3).
- **We deliver:** the base choice only. The Enhancement reaches the player as description prose. Worse, because the record carries no `enhancement` field, `build.ts:4700` skips it — so `lesser-augmentation` and `greater-augmentation` **cannot even list Hardened Chassis as a target**, and both carry a note telling the player to apply it by hand.
- **The lane already exists and works:** `build.ts:4695-4726` resolves the augmentation picker and applies `enhancement.grant`, with `enhancement.choiceIds` gating a tier-only sub-question. Six automaton feats use it (`automaton-armament`, `arcane-communication`, `arcane-eye`, `automaton-lore`, `powerful-tail`, `undead-hunter`). Hardened Chassis was simply never authored into it.
- **Fix:** add an `enhancement` block to `feats/hardened-chassis` in `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json`, shaped like `automaton-lore`'s — `enhancement.choiceIds: ['<new effectChoices id>']` plus a **two-option** `effectChoices` group: (A) `{ type: 'physical', value: 3, condition: 'except against adamantine weapons and unarmed attacks' }`, (B) the already-chosen type raised to `max(3, floor(@actor.level/2))`. Then change the Hardened Chassis option note on both augmentation feats from the "read it and apply it in play" wording to the "Computed on your sheet" wording the other six use.
- **⚠ Trap:** do **not** author it as a one-option picker — `resolvePick` auto-applies a lone unanswered option (`build.ts:4558`), which would grant the tier to every automaton that never took an Augmentation feat.

---

**4. `spirit-warrior-dedication` — the fist is still 1d4 and has no parry** (KINDS + IDENTITY)

- **They deliver:** a pre-modified fist — 1d6, brawling, **with the parry trait** — plus the waived lethal-attack penalty and the granted action.
- **We deliver:** verified in `public/core.json` — `unarmedTraits` is exactly `[{ remove: ['nonlethal'] }]`. Nothing else. One of three printed clauses lands. `spirit-warrior` appears nowhere in `src/`; the only die upgrade in the engine is `derive.ts:4511`, keyed on `powerful-fist` (the monk feature), which never fires here.
- **⚠ The two audits disagreed on the fix — resolved:** the KINDS audit said `stepDie: true`, the IDENTITY audit said `setDie: 'd6'`. **`setDie` is correct.** I confirmed it exists on `UnarmedRider` (`src/rules/types.ts:571`) and is read at `derive.ts:4397`/`4404`, and the type's own comment says it wins over `stepDie` "since it states a result rather than a change". The printed clause states a result, and `setDie` is also safe against double-stepping if another effect steps the same die.
- **Fix:** in `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json`, replace the `unarmedTraits` value for this id with
  `[{ match: ['fist'], setDie: 'd6', add: ['parry'] }, { remove: ['nonlethal'] }]`
  — first rider narrowed to the fist for die and trait, second left unmatched so the lethal-penalty clause keeps covering all unarmed attacks as printed. No engine change needed. Also update `scripts/backfill-residual-1-12.mjs:118`, which writes the same value and will otherwise reintroduce the old one.

---

**5. `ghostly-resistance` — the resistance against non-magical damage is roughly half what it should be** (VALUES)

- **They deliver:** two resistance entries — the general one at 1/2/3, **and** a separate non-magical-source resistance at 2/4/5.
- **We deliver:** one entry. Verified in `core.json`: a single `all-damage` resistance at `floor((@actor.level+2)/6)` with the force/vitality/ghost-touch exception. Correct for the first half; the doubled non-magical ladder has no carrier anywhere — no second row, no situational star, no note. Grepping the id across `src/` returns zero hits.
- **The justification never mentioned this half at all** — it only ever argued about exception-in-the-type-string vs exception-as-condition. See §2.
- **⚠ FIX AS WRITTEN IS WRONG:** the original suggested fix contains a self-contradiction (it proposes `type:'physical'` and then says that is wrong) and proposes `2 * floor(...)`, which yields 2/4/**6** — the printed ladder is 2/4/**5**.
- **Fix:** add a second entry to `feats/ghostly-resistance.resistances` in `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json` with the same `all-damage` type, an explicit level-mapped formula producing **2 at levels 4-9, 4 at 10-15, 5 at 16+** (not a clean double), and a condition stating it applies against non-magical sources and still excludes force, vitality and ghost touch. Confirm the two rows surface as separate lines in the IWR breakdown rather than merging.

---

### P2 — the player gets the wrong thing, or an option that delivers nothing

---

**6. `elemental-wrath` — the grant points at a retired spell record with different mechanics** (IDENTITY)

- **They deliver:** an at-will innate primal cantrip in its current printing — 5-foot burst at 30 feet, basic Reflex, 1d8, +1d8 every 2 ranks, retyped to the chosen energy.
- **We deliver:** verified in `core.json` — both the flat `innateSpells` grant and all four `effectChoices` branches point at `acid-splash`, which our own corpus stamps `edition: 'superseded'`: a single-target **spell attack**, 1d6 plus splash plus persistent on a crit, fixed heightening at 3/5/7/9. `caustic-blast` ships alongside it as `edition: 'remaster'` with the burst/save/1d8 shape. `build.ts:2382-2384` states superseded records are always hidden from pickers — so this grant hands the player a record the app otherwise refuses to offer.
- **Fix:** in `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json`, repoint `innateSpells[0].spellId`, all four `effectChoices` option grants, and the `spellNotes` entry's `spellId` from `acid-splash` to `caustic-blast`.
- **Two extras I found while verifying, fix in the same pass:**
  - the flat `innateSpells[0]` entry carries `atWill: true` but **no `heightenHalfLevel`**, while all four `effectChoices` grants do — so the unanswered-picker path yields a cantrip that never scales. Add it.
  - the record carries **both** a `choice` with flag `element` **and** an `effectChoices` group with id `element`. These are stored in different maps (`build.choiceFlags` vs `build.effectChoices['<recordId>:<choiceId>']`) and are rendered by different controls, so this is very likely the same duplicate-prompt shape as item 7 — two questions asking for one damage type, answerable inconsistently. Mechanically harmless today (both branches grant the same spell id and the retype is prose-only), but it should be collapsed to one picker. **Verify by building before removing either.**
- **Guard:** assert no `innateSpells` grant anywhere in the corpus points at a spell whose `edition` is `superseded`.

---

**7. `the-moon-weavers-art` — two prompts for one clause, and a player who answers both gets two spells** (KINDS)

- **They deliver:** one occult innate spell, once per day, chosen from the two the clause names.
- **We deliver:** the record's own `effectChoices` picker (`moon-weavers-spell`, verified in `core.json`) **and** a second, redundant picker from the entry still sitting at `src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts:98`. `Builder.tsx:2172-2192` renders both; `build.ts` pushes both answers into `innateGrants` (`:6128-6130` and `:6132-6150`), deduping only by spell id. Measured: answer one picker Illusory Object and the other Invisible Item and the innate entry comes back holding **both** at rank 1. This is an over-delivery — we give a player more than the printed rule.
- **Fix:** delete the `'the-moon-weavers-art'` entry from `src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts`. The record's `effectChoices` (authored in `scripts/backfill-batch15.mjs:260` → `effect-backfill.json:142302`) is the keeper.
- **⚠ Durability trap — the deletion will regress if you only edit the .ts file.** That registry entry originates from `scripts/audit/patches.jsonl:335`, and `scripts/audit/apply-patches.ts:427-429` **rewrites `featCantripGrants.ts` whole** from the patch list. Remove or neutralise the `patches.jsonl` row in the same commit. (I confirmed the record carries no `spellNotes`, so removing the registry entry will not trip the `fromCantripPick` check at `scripts/apply-innate-cantrip-lane.mjs:251`.)
- **Guard:** refuse any record that appears in `FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS` **and** carries an `effectChoices` option granting `innateSpells`. This is a general shape, not a one-off — worth running across the whole registry now.

---

**8. `ascended-dragonet-heritage` — one of five options delivers nothing** (KINDS)

- **They deliver:** all five options' full mechanical content, including the drake option's at-will arcane cantrip.
- **We deliver:** speeds, languages and creature traits from the named heritage — but no innate spells. `src/rules/build.ts:6083-6087` reads heritage `innateSpells` from `build.heritageId` **only**; `secondHeritageId` is missing from that one loop, unlike the sibling loops at `:3033`, `:4729`, `:5469` and `:5928`. Measured: naming Homing Drake produces no spellcasting entry at all.
- **Fix (one line):** at `src/rules/build.ts:6083`, use the `for (const hid of [build.heritageId, secondHeritageId])` shape the four sibling loops already use.
- **Blast radius — this is why it ranks above its own severity:** the bug is in the *engine*, not the record. Any second-heritage source pointing at a heritage with `innateSpells` is silently dropping it. After the fix, re-check every record that sets `secondHeritage: true`.
- **Guard:** a test asserting that a character whose second heritage carries `innateSpells` receives them.

---

**9. `stylish-tricks` — the swashbuckler cannot take the feat the rule reserves for them** (KINDS)

- **They deliver:** at 3rd/7th/15th, a bonus skill feat drawn from Acrobatics **or** the skill the chosen style granted — so a Braggart can slot an Intimidation feat, a Battledancer a Performance feat.
- **We deliver:** Acrobatics feats only, plus feats naming no skill. Every style skill is filtered *out* of the slot.
- **Root cause — a write-only field, confirmed by grep:** `classes/swashbuckler.restrictedSkillFeatLevels` sets `includeSubclassGrantedSkills: true`, and **that flag has no reader**. Across the whole tree it appears exactly three times: the type declaration at `src/rules/types.ts:3145`, the authored value at `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:134569`, and the baked copy in `public/core.json`. The only consumer, `src/rules/featSlots.ts:183-192`, builds its allowed set from `restrict.skills` + `restrict.abilities` and never looks at the flag. Swashbuckler sets no abilities list, so `allowed = {acrobatics}`.
- **Not covered by the owner's picker exception:** that exception covers *where* we filter, not filtering out options the printed rule allows.
- **Fix:** in `src/rules/featSlots.ts`, inside the `restrictedSkillFeatLevels` block (~:186), when `restrict.includeSubclassGrantedSkills` is set, add the skills granted by the character's chosen subclass option (`core.json classes/<id>.subclass.options[].grants.skills`) to `allowed` before the `named.some()` test. Investigator carries the same flag and needs the same treatment for correctness, even though its ability list already covers every methodology skill.
- **Guard:** the standing dead-reader sweep should have caught this one. Whatever query it uses, extend it to flags declared in `types.ts` and authored in `effect-backfill.json` with no `src/` read site.

---

### P3 — a number one or two steps off

---

**10. `colugos-traversal` — the spell never heightens, and the lane it sits in cannot heighten anything** (KINDS)

- **They deliver:** the chosen spell at 3rd rank from 9th level, with the innate DC/attack stepping to expert at 12th.
- **We deliver:** the chosen spell at base rank 1 at every level from 5 to 20. Only the expert step arrives. Verified: `feats/colugos-traversal` carries **no mechanical fields at all** in `core.json` — the whole feat is the registry entry at `featCantripGrants.ts:59`. `CantripPickSpec` has no rank or heighten field of any kind (I read the full interface), and the file header states outright that feat heightening is not modelled.
- **The justification claimed "ours carries `heightenHalfLevel` on the grant" — it does not.** See §2.
- **Recommended fix — move it off the pick lane, don't extend the lane.** Author `effectChoices` on the record in `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json` with two options, each granting `innateSpells` with `heightenAt: [{ level: 9, rank: 3 }]`. `heightenAt` is a real field on the innate-grant type (`types.ts:2059`) and is read at `build.ts:6199`; this route needs no engine change and no serialiser change. Then delete the `featCantripGrants` entry — **and its `patches.jsonl` row**, per the trap in item 7.
- **⚠ If you instead add a field to `CantripPickSpec`:** the file's own header warns that `scripts/aon-verify/apply-clear.ts` rewrites it whole through a serialiser (`scripts/aon-verify/_ser.ts`) and deletes anything the serialiser does not emit. You must add the field there too. This is why the effectChoices route is the safer one.
- **⚠ SYSTEMIC — this is not one record.** I checked the base ranks of every pick-lane entry whose prompt names a rank. Three are wrong today, not one:
  - `kitsune-spell-expertise` — printed 5th-rank; `confusion` ships at base rank **4**. A kitsune choosing Confusion casts it a rank low.
  - `spiritual-echo` — printed 4th-rank; four of the five options (`spirit-sense`, `status`, `darkness`, `blood-vendetta`) ship at base rank **2**. Two ranks low.
  - `colugos-traversal` — as above.
  - (`transcendent-realization`, `basic-skysage-divination`, `apprentice-sea-witch`, `mask-of-power` all check out — every option's base rank already matches the printed rank.)
  - `reclaimant-plea` and `words-of-unraveling` have options spanning multiple base ranks; I could not confirm their printed rank. Worth a look in the same pass.
  - **Guard:** for every `FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS` entry whose prompt names an ordinal rank, assert every option's base rank equals it.

---

**11. `animistic-practice` — the Medium is short a focus point at levels 9-14** (KINDS, medium confidence)

- **They deliver:** a Medium-practice animist at 9th+ gets one extra focus point, suppressed if they already have Circle of Spirits — 3 points at levels 9-14.
- **We deliver:** 2 points, identical to every other practice. `build.ts:3681-3702` has only the flat 1/7/15 ladder plus the `focusSeen.has('circle-of-spirits')` clause. `classes.animist.subclass.options['medium']` carries description prose and no grant. Nothing reads the practice choice.
- **The justification's premise is false:** it claimed a `focus` field on a class feature is not read. It is — `build.ts:3008` sums `focusPoolBonus` over `classFeatureIdsOwned`, which includes the chosen subclass id, and `build.ts:3702` adds it to the animist pool. The Medium option could have carried it all along.
- **Fix (preferred, no code):** author `focusPoolBonus` on the medium subclass record — `build.ts:3008` already reads it. If the level-9 gate and the Circle of Spirits suppression cannot be expressed on the record, add a Medium branch beside the existing Circle of Spirits clause in `build.ts` (~:3690) instead.
- **Needs a ruling before it can be written correctly** — see §3.

---

### P4 — nothing delivered but blocked, or a surfacing gap

---

**12. `merchants-scale` — delivers nothing, and would still deliver nothing if authored today** (VALUES)

- **They deliver:** a +1 to seven knowledge skills, each conditioned to Recall Knowledge about the value of items, gems and precious metals.
- **We deliver:** nothing. `items/merchants-scale` ships an empty description, no `situational` entry, no skill grant.
- **Why a naive fix would not work:** an item's situational bonuses are admitted only while the row is equipped/worn/invested, and no equip control renders for an untraited `equipment` item. Authoring the stars alone leaves them inert.
- **Recorded as DIVERGENT rather than AUTHORISED deliberately:** the half of the justification about not copying their sentence is genuinely correct and should stand. But the settle silenced seven keys and the player receives zero across all of them, and it fits none of the three authorised grounds — we cannot read the printed text, so their data cannot be *shown* to contradict it, and there is no star to point at.
- **Fix, strictly in this order:** (1) add a Hold/Use route in `src/sheet/InventoryTab.tsx` for `equipment`-typed items whose `usage` is `held-in-*`, or everything downstream is inert; (2) source the printed paragraph — **owner action, see §3**; (3) add one starred conditional per named skill under `'merchants-scale'` in `FEAT_SITUATIONAL` (`src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts`), in the `merchants-guile` shape.

---

**13. `spellshifter-dedication` — the archetype's action never reaches the sheet** (KINDS + IDENTITY)

- **They deliver:** a named one-action ability on the character sheet, carrying the action's rules with the archetype's spellshift folded in — an action with an action cost, in the action list.
- **We deliver:** the dedication plus a one-line note. Verified: the id returns **zero hits across all of `src/`** — no registry entry, no branch in `derive.ts` or `build.ts`, nothing in `effect-backfill.json`. Only three records carry this archetype and none has `grantsActions`.
- **The justification's facts are all correct** — the action genuinely is absent from our corpus, and the only similarly-named record is a level-14 wizard feat about moving a spell's area, so pointing at it would be the defect. But "the record does not exist" describes the gap; it does not make the player whole.
- **Fix:** author an `actions` record for the archetype's shift action (1 action, concentrate + manipulate, with the Arcana-check text) plus the archetype's spellshift, marked `aonOrigin: 'authored'` — the same route already used for the werecreature battle forms and `stances/haft-striker-stance` — then set `grantsActions: ['<new id>']` on the dedication. The lane is live on 148 feat records pointing into the 879-entry `actions` bucket.
- **⚠ Do not** reinstate any grant pointing at the wizard feat with the colliding name.

---

**14. `zombie-dedication` — a printed clause of the undead package is never shown** (IDENTITY, medium confidence)

- **They deliver:** the shared undead-benefits package, including the survival clause (at 0 HP you are knocked out and start dying as the living do; stabilising and similar recoveries do not work on you; being reduced to death destroys you).
- **We deliver:** the five mechanical clauses all land correctly (death-effect immunity, +1 circumstance vs disease and poison, Necril, negative healing, the jaws strike, and the fist's nonlethal removal — all verified in the record). But the survival clause appears nowhere. I scanned every record in `core.json`: that text sits on exactly **five** dedications — ghost, ghoul, lich, mummy, vampire. Zombie's single `note` slot is occupied by the jaws grabbed/restrained restriction instead, and `core.rules['basic-undead-benefits']` is a stub with no entry in `core-descriptions.json`, so there is no second route to it.
- **Fix:** carry the survival sentence on `feats.zombie-dedication` via `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json` (anything not authored there dies at the next `npm run data`). Either append it to the existing `note`, or move the jaws restriction onto the `grantedStrikes` entry to free the slot — **verify a per-strike note field exists and renders before choosing the second route**; the strike entry currently carries only `name`/`die`/`damageType`/`traits`/`group`.
- **Guard:** assert that every feat carrying `negativeHealing` together with `grantsLanguages: ['necril']` also states the survival clause. That is what would have caught the sixth going missing.

## 2. Landmines — settles that are right by accident, or whose reasoning is false

These do not all need code, but every one of them needs its justification comment rewritten, because the next person to read it will be misled.

| Record | What the justification asserts | What is actually true |
|---|---|---|
| **`second-implement`** (withdrawn, verdict stands) | "the initiate benefit comes from the implement record" | It comes from a **sibling** record keyed off the implement id — `classFeatures/initiate-benefit-<imp>`, thirty of them across ten implements. The implement records themselves carry no grants and their tier headings are empty *by design*. The mechanical claim is true and the settle stands, but anyone who follows the stated reasoning will open `classFeatures/amulet`, find nothing, and conclude the app is broken. **Rewrite the comment to name `build.ts:6408-6440` and the `initiate-benefit-*` records.** |
| **`colugos-traversal`** | "ours carries `heightenHalfLevel` on the grant" | It does not. I grepped `heightenHalfLevel` across `src/`, `scripts/` and `core.json`: 339 records carry it, none of them this one. The justification also quotes a different feat's heightening sentence. |
| **`ghostly-resistance`** | argues only about exception-in-the-type-string vs exception-as-condition | Correct as far as it goes, and entirely beside the point — it never mentions the doubled non-magical value, which is the whole divergence. A settle that silences a key by discussing a different property of it. |
| **`animistic-practice`** | "a `focus` field on a class feature is not read" | False. `build.ts:3008` reads `focusPoolBonus` off owned class features including the subclass id, and `build.ts:3702` feeds it into the animist pool. The settle was justified by a capability gap that does not exist. |
| **`hardened-chassis`** | "an upgrade is the upgrading record's business" | The upgrading records (`lesser-augmentation`, `greater-augmentation`) explicitly do *not* deliver it — they carry a note telling the player to apply it by hand, and `build.ts:4700` skips any answer whose feat has no `enhancement`, so they cannot even list it. |
| **`firework-technician-dedication`** | `advancedAlchemy { items: 4 }` stands in for "the printed 4 made during daily preparations" | Wrong subsystem. The printed 4 are versatile vials; Advanced Alchemy prepared items are a separate resource with a separate panel. The settle silenced a real gap by naming a number that happened to match. |
| **`spirit-warrior-dedication`** | "our `unarmedTraits` rider steps the die and adds parry" | The rider is `[{ remove: ['nonlethal'] }]` and nothing else. True about the shape, false about the content — one of three clauses. |
| **`zombie-dedication`** | the inlined package "matches clause for clause", listing six clauses | Five. The sixth is absent from this record and present on the other five undead dedications. |
| **`merchants-scale`** | "this settle closes the +1, not the description" | Accurately describes what the backlog file says, and the file itself calls the gap "its own defect". The settle silences seven keys on a record that delivers nothing. |

**Pattern worth acting on:** six of the nine above silence a real gap by making a *true statement about a neighbouring fact*. A justification that names a field, a registry or a number is not evidence unless it also names the read site. Consider requiring every new settle comment to cite a `file:line` read site, and adding a check that the cited path exists.

## 3. Needs the project owner

No settle came back UNSURE. These six decisions surfaced *inside* confirmed divergences and the engineer cannot resolve them alone. Printed text is cited by record id rather than reproduced.

**a. `merchants-scale` — the printed paragraph cannot be sourced by this project.**
The AoN mirror docs, live AoN, and the Foundry record are all stat-block stubs with no body; their dump is GPL-3.0 and off limits. The paragraph must be transcribed from the physical Player Core (pg. 290) by the owner. Until then step (3) of the fix cannot be written, and adopting their flat +1 verbatim remains ruled out. **Question: transcribe it, or leave the item inert and reopen the settle as a known gap?**

**b. `animistic-practice` — how to read the Medium's pool rule.**
Printed (see `core-descriptions.json`, the medium practice / Dual Invocation text): the pool equals the number of focus spells *or* the number of primary apparitions, whichever is higher, capped at 3. Their side encodes it as a flat +1 point at 9th, suppressed by Circle of Spirits. The proposed fix (`Math.max(poolMax, pointCostingKnown.length, 2)`) lands the same number in the common case but is an interpretation, not a transcription. **Question: match their flat +1 gated at 9th, or implement the "whichever is higher" reading?** The two-primary-apparitions half of the clause is unmodelled either way and would be a separate work item.

**c. `gates-threshold` — the fork-branch impulse filter.**
The printed clause says an impulse feat of your level or lower with that element's trait. The "non-composite" narrowing comes from their encoding, not from a sentence I can point at. **Question: apply the non-composite exclusion, or offer every element-matched impulse at or below level?**

**d. `hardened-chassis` — whether the Enhancement should be a visible tier question.**
The printed Enhancement is itself a two-way branch, so authoring it means adding a second prompt that only appears once an Augmentation feat points at this feat. That is more UI than the other six enhancement feats have. Per the standing rule I am not asking where to put the control — but **whether the app should surface a conditional sub-prompt at all** is a shape question the six existing records do not settle.

**e. `zombie-dedication` — one note slot, two clauses.**
The record has a single `note` and it is spent on the jaws restriction. Options: concatenate both into one note; add a note field to `grantedStrikes` entries; or fill in the `basic-undead-benefits` rules stub and route all six dedications through it. The third is the architecturally right answer and the largest. **Question: which?**

**f. `elemental-wrath` — the duplicate `element` question.**
The record carries both a `choice` with flag `element` and an `effectChoices` group with id `element`, stored in different maps and rendered by different controls. Collapsing them is almost certainly correct but changes an existing saved-character answer key. **Question: collapse now, or leave both and only fix the spell repoint?** (The spell repoint is unblocked either way and should not wait on this.)
